newsitem.title: NORWAY: North Sea oil output to rise 7 pct in 1997-WoodMac.
newsitem.headline: North Sea oil output to rise 7 pct in 1997-WoodMac.

text.p: North Sea oil production will increase next year by an estimated seven percent over 1996 to an average 6.47 million barrels per day (bpd), according to a forecast by analysts Wood Mackenzie.
Wood Mackenzie said the additional 400,000 bpd would come from record output in Norway, Britain and Denmark. Only in the Netherlands was production forecast to fall.
Norwegian oil output was expected to rise by six percent in 1997 to average 3.43 million bpd, although it would peak at more than 3.60 million bpd by year-end, the Edinburgh-based analysts said.
Six new fields, including Norne and Vigdis, and output increases at Draugen, Heidrun and Troll would contribute to the extra flow.
"Strong production performances from the Snorre, Ekofisk, Oseberg and Gullfaks fields are also expected," they said.
Latest estimates suggest Norway will pump an average 3.25 million bpd in 1996, up 12 percent from 1995.
Crude production in the British sector of the North Sea was projected to rise by around five percent, or some 210,000 bpd, to a record 2.78 million bpd in 1997 as 11 new fields are brought onstream.
Wood Mackenzie said the impact of scheduled maintenance shutdowns on British output next year would be more marked than in 1996, assuming the recent cycle of biannual programme holds.
Three fields would stop producing altogether.
"We estimate that production will cease from the Donan, Glamis and Heather fields which currently produce around 13,000 bpd," they said.
Danish production was forecast to increase to a record 224,000 bpd.

"The combination of these changes plus the six percent increase in output from Norway will result in a 400,000 bpd increase in total output from the North Sea to an average 6.47 million bpd in 1997," Wood Mackenzie said.
